title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error is detectable. The exact identification of SR_{ρ,σ} ≃ T^+_{ρ,σ} with a product (read as S'T_ρ × SN'_σ) is illegible and may be misread. The asymmetry between ρ and σ in that product is suspicious and would need checking against (103)–(107).
Numbering issue: the next page also uses (118) for a different formula, so Grothendieck reuses equation numbers.

ideas.what: Cube of algebraic groups linked by G_m-, SG-, PG-torsors and μ2×μ2 component extensions, with cartesian lateral faces
ideas.modern_name: Commutative cube of central extensions / torsors; cartesian squares of group schemes
ideas.where_published: Not in this form; the general tools are in SGA3

ideas.what: Middle terms of one face are trivial products (torsor trivial); the opposite face becomes trivial after passing to a pro-covering of the middle terms
ideas.modern_name: Trivialisation of torsors after pullback to a (pro-)étale / isogeny cover

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bookkeeping page inside a long computational exploration: a diagram of groups attached to the 'loop equation' and the remark that certain torsors split after a pro-covering. The work is routine relative to standard group-scheme theory, with no evident new result or uncaptured connection.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top reads '523'; the previous page transcription '572' is likely a misreading of 522.

Likely reading: 'C'est presque le cas aussi pour la face parallèle (face postérieure droite), ou plus précisément – cela devient vrai à condition de remplacer les termes médians M_{ρ,σ}, M°_{ρ,σ} par les pro-revêtements' rather than 'C'est pourquoi le cas ...'.
In (118) the tildes sit over the M's: \tilde M_{ρ,σ} ≃ R_{ρ,σ} × SG, \tilde M°_{ρ,σ} ≃ R°_{ρ,σ} × SG.
In the diagram, M^+_{ρ,σ} is annotated '≃ SR_{ρ,σ} × [SG]', and the T's are written with a script tau (τ_{ρ,σ}), consistent with the next page.
